reading: A small multi-colour pattern sits at the left edge. It is copied to the right edge, and the gap between the two copies is filled in each row with that row's first (and last) pattern colour.
verb: copy pattern to opposite edge and bridge

slots.unit: the fg block at the left edge (input width-independent)
slots.copy_place: flush against the right border, same rows
slots.gap_fill: each row between the copies takes the colour of that row's first pattern cell

why: output = left pattern + per-row fill + same pattern at right edge; pattern's first and last columns are equal

reading: Each solid 8 rectangle is repainted: its four half-by-half quadrants become 6 (top-left), 1 (top-right), 2 (bottom-left), 3 (bottom-right), and the interior inset 2 cells from every edge becomes 4.

slots.subject: each 8 rectangle object
slots.quadrant_colours: TL 6, TR 1, BL 2, BR 3 (split at half height and half width)
slots.core: cells at least 2 from the rectangle's edge become 4

why: every rectangle cell is recoloured by its position inside its own rectangle; background unchanged

reading: Two opposite border lines of different colours bound the grid. Every 1 cell gets one neighbour cell (on the side facing the nearer border line) painted with that line's colour.
verb: mark side toward nearest border line

slots.subject: each isolated 1 cell
slots.direction: orthogonal step toward the nearer of the two full border lines
slots.colour: colour of that nearer border line

why: each 1 cell gains exactly one adjacent cell coloured like the closer border line, on the side facing it

reading: Every object moves right by a distance equal to its own bounding-box width, keeping its shape.
why: each object reappears unchanged, displaced right by its width

reading: Several overlapping, partly hidden octagon rings of different colours (plus scattered noise cells) lie on a background. Each ring is completed to the same 6x6 octagon outline and the rings are stacked vertically in a 6-wide output.

slots.subject: each ring colour (ignoring the scattered noise colours)
slots.shape: the fixed 6x6 octagon ring, background elsewhere
slots.order: vertical stacking order of the rings (likely by layering/occlusion; uncertain)

why: output height = 6 x number of rings; each 6x6 block is the complete ring of one colour on the input background

reading: A 2x2 block of four colours in the centre is pushed outward: each cell moves to the grid corner on its own side, and the centre becomes empty.

slots.subject: the four cells of the central 2x2 block
slots.target: the grid corner diagonal from each cell (TL->TL corner, etc.)

why: the four colours appear exactly at the four grid corners in the same relative arrangement; all else background
invariants: the four colours and their relative arrangement

reading: Green (3) cells that touch another 3 cell orthogonally turn 8; lone 3 cells (no orthogonal 3 neighbour) stay 3.

new_rows.name: paired
new_rows.datalog:
paired(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0, off(DY, DX), DY = 0, X2 = X + DX, px(Y, X2, C).
paired(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C > 0, off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, px(Y2, X, C).

why: every non-zero cell with a same-colour orthogonal neighbour maps 3 -> 8; everything else unchanged (note: 3 is the majority colour in some pairs, so px with C > 0 is used instead of cell)

reading: A horizontal and a vertical line cross. A 3x3 square ring of 4 is drawn around the crossing cell, overwriting the line cells there; the crossing cell itself keeps its colour.

new_rows.name: crossing
new_rows.datalog: crossing(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Ya = Y - 1, Yb = Y + 1, Xa = X - 1, Xb = X + 1, cell(Ya, X, C1), cell(Yb, X, C2), cell(Y, Xa, C3), cell(Y, Xb, C4).

why: the unit is a 3x3 ring of 4 with a transparent centre, centred on the one cell whose four orthogonal neighbours are all non-background

reading: Two 3x3 boxes of 2 with a 5 centre each have one gap in their wall. The gaps are filled with 4 and a thick 4-coloured band is drawn joining the two gaps, running through the background between the boxes (bounded by the box strips on the non-gap sides).
verb: join box openings with a band

slots.openings: the missing wall cell of each box
slots.band: background cells of the box spanned by the cells just outside the two openings, excluding each box's row/column strip on its closed side

why: only background cells (and the two gap cells) change, all to 4, forming one connected region touching both gaps

reading: From the 2 cell on the bottom row a two-cell-wide staircase of 2 climbs diagonally up-right to the top/right border; when a 1 cell blocks the path the staircase steps around it and continues.

slots.source: the 2 cell on the bottom row
slots.path: diagonal up-right staircase, two cells per row (current column and next)
slots.obstacles: 1 cells, which are kept and detoured around

why: only background cells change, all to 2, forming a staircase from the 2 to the border that never covers a 1
